revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Presidential Terms
revealWordProblem.text: A presidential term in the United States is four years. In 1947, Congress passed an amendment to limit the president to two terms. The number of terms served by each president of the United States from 1789 to 2021 is shown in the bar graph. Given this information, what prediction can you make about the number of terms the next U.S. president will serve in office?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The bar graph shows: less than 1 term = 7 presidents, 1 term = 18, between 1 and 2 terms = 3, 2 terms = 15, more than 2 terms = 1. That's 7 + 18 + 3 + 15 + 1 = 44 presidents total. The tallest bar, and the mode of the data, is '1 term' with 18 out of 44 presidents, or 18 ÷ 44 ≈ 0.409 = 40.9% — the largest share of any category. Also, since the 1947 amendment now caps presidents at two terms, 'more than 2 terms' is no longer possible for future presidents. Based on this data, the most likely prediction is that the next U.S. president will serve 1 term.

vocabulary.definition: A mean, median, or mode chosen because it describes a data set fairly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una media, mediana o moda elegida porque describe un conjunto de datos de manera justa.
vocabulary.visual: Use the median when an outlier would pull the mean too far.
vocabulary.cloze: A center chosen because it describes the data fairly is an ___ ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Using the median when one salary is $40 million
examples.why: The outlier drags the mean; the median stays with the group.

examples.text: Using the mean in that same data set
examples.why: One extreme value pulls it away from every actual salary.

vocabulary.definition: The average. Add all the numbers, then divide by how many there are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El promedio. Suma todos los números y divide entre cuántos hay.
vocabulary.cloze: The average of a data set is the ___.

examples.why: Add the values, then divide by how many there are.
That is the total; the mean still needs the division.

vocabulary.definition: The middle number when you put them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El número del medio cuando los pones en orden.
vocabulary.cloze: The middle value when data is in order, often best when there is an outlier, is the ___.

examples.why: The middle value once the numbers are in order.
Middle of an unsorted list is not the median.

vocabulary.definition: A number that is much bigger or smaller than the rest.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número mucho mayor o menor que los demás.
vocabulary.visual: Data: 12, 14, 13, 15, 45 → 45 is far from the cluster, so it is an outlier
vocabulary.cloze: A value far from the rest of the data, which can pull the mean, is an ___.

examples.why: It sits far from every other value.
It is the largest, but it is right beside the others.

vocabulary.definition: When most data sits on one side with a tail on the other.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuando la mayoría de los datos está de un lado con una cola del otro.
vocabulary.visual: Scores: 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 35 → most scores are low, but 35 creates a tail to the right (skewed right)
vocabulary.cloze: Data that is bunched on one side with a tail on the other is ___.

examples.text: Most values low with a few very high values
examples.why: The data has a tail, so it is skewed.

examples.text: Values spread evenly around the center

vocabulary.definition: How the data looks: where it sits and how spread out it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cómo se ven los datos: dónde están y qué tan separados están.
vocabulary.visual: Symmetric = even on both sides. Skewed = bunched on one side with a tail
vocabulary.cloze: The way data values are spread out is the ___.

examples.text: “Most scores cluster near 85, with one down at 68”
examples.why: It says where the data sits and how it spreads.

vocabulary.definition: How spread out the numbers are.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están los números.
vocabulary.cloze: How much the data values differ is the ___.

examples.why: The values differ, which is what variability measures.
Nothing varies, so there is no spread to describe.

conceptIntro.heading: Should I use the mean or the median?
conceptIntro.intro: The mean and the median both describe the center of a data set, but one fits better depending on the shape. When the data has an outlier (a value far from the rest), the median is usually the better choice.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Choosing Appropriate Measures of Center & Spread. 1. Symmetric Data (No Outliers): Use Mean and MAD. 2. Skewed Data (Has Outliers): Use Median and IQR (outliers distort the mean). 3. Compare distributions using both center (typical value) and spread (variability)

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My data, the top scorer's points: 22, 24, 20, 25, 23, 21, 58. I notice 58 is much bigger than the rest, so it is an outlier.

The mean (27.6) is higher than 6 of the 7 games because 58 pulled it up. So the median (23) better shows a typical game.

optionalActivity.name: Best Measure Decision Cards
optionalActivity.intro: You are the team's data analyst — read each scouting question and pick the measure that answers it best.

optional.stem: A scout records points per game: 14, 16, 15, 17, 16, 58. To report a TYPICAL game, which measure of center is best?
choices: Median, because 58 is an outlier that pulls the mean up
Mean, because it uses every game
Range, because it shows the highest game
Mode, because 16 appears twice
optional.explanation: The 58-point game is an outlier. It pulls the mean above 5 of the 6 games, so the median (16) better shows a typical game.
choiceFeedback: The mean is pulled higher by 58—does that show a typical game?
Range is 44—does that describe typical, or spread?
16 appears twice—is mode about a typical game when there's an outlier?
optional.stemEs: Un observador registra los puntos por partido: 14, 16, 15, 17, 16, 58. Para informar un partido TÍPICO, ¿cuál medida de centro es la mejor?
optional.explanationEs: El partido de 58 puntos es un valor atípico. Jala la media por encima de 5 de los 6 partidos, así que la mediana (16) muestra mejor un partido típico.
hints: A typical value should sit near most of the data instead of being pulled by one unusual game.
Scan for an outlier first, then choose the measure that an outlier does not drag around.
Put the scores in order: 14, 15, 16, 16, 17, 58. Compare where the middle of that list sits to where the average of all six would land.
hintsEs: Un valor típico debe quedar cerca de la mayoría de los datos y no ser jalado por un solo partido poco común.
Busca primero un valor atípico y después elige la medida que un valor atípico no arrastra.
Ordena las puntuaciones: 14, 15, 16, 16, 17, 58. Compara dónde queda el centro de esa lista con dónde caería el promedio de los seis.
choicesEs: La mediana, porque 58 es un valor atípico que sube la media
La media, porque usa todos los partidos
El rango, porque muestra el partido más alto
La moda, porque 16 aparece dos veces

optional.stem: The equipment manager needs to order the MOST COMMON jersey size from this list: M, L, M, S, M, L, M. Which measure answers the question?
choices: Mode, because it names the value that appears most
Mean, because it averages the sizes
Median, because it finds the middle size
Range, because it shows the size gap
optional.explanation: The mode is the value that shows up most often. Here size M appears 4 times, so the mode (M) tells the manager what to order most.
choiceFeedback: Average size doesn't make sense—which size appears most?
Median finds the middle order—which size shows up most?
Range is the spread—which size do you order most?
optional.stemEs: El encargado del equipo necesita pedir la talla de camiseta MÁS COMÚN de esta lista: M, L, M, S, M, L, M. ¿Cuál medida responde la pregunta?
optional.explanationEs: La moda es el valor que aparece con más frecuencia. Aquí la talla M aparece 4 veces, así que la moda (M) le dice al encargado qué pedir en mayor cantidad.
hints: Sizes like S, M, and L are categories, not numbers you can add or average.
Ask which measure of center reports the value that appears most often.
Count how many times each size shows up in M, L, M, S, M, L, M and see which count comes out largest.
hintsEs: Las tallas como S, M y L son categorías, no números que se puedan sumar o promediar.
Pregúntate cuál medida de centro informa el valor que aparece con más frecuencia.
Cuenta cuántas veces aparece cada talla en M, L, M, S, M, L, M y observa cuál conteo resulta mayor.
choicesEs: La moda, porque nombra el valor que aparece más veces
La media, porque promedia las tallas
La mediana, porque encuentra la talla del medio
El rango, porque muestra la diferencia de tallas

optional.stem: A coach wants to know how SPREAD OUT the team's free-throw makes are: 6, 7, 6, 8, 18. Which measure of spread is most affected by the lone 18?
choices: Range, because it is the highest minus the lowest value
Median, because it is in the middle
Mode, because it is the most common
Mean absolute deviation only, never the range
optional.explanation: Range = max − min = 18 − 6 = 12. Because it uses only the two most extreme values, one outlier (18) changes the range a lot.
choiceFeedback: Median finds middle—does it measure spread?
Mode is most common—does it measure spread?
MAD measures spread—but range is most affected by one extreme value.
optional.stemEs: Un entrenador quiere saber qué tan DISPERSOS están los tiros libres encestados del equipo: 6, 7, 6, 8, 18. ¿Cuál medida de dispersión se ve más afectada por el único 18?
optional.explanationEs: Rango = máximo − mínimo = 18 − 6 = 12. Como usa solamente los dos valores más extremos, un solo valor atípico (18) cambia mucho el rango.
hints: Measures of spread describe how far apart the values are, not where the center sits.
Look for the measure that is calculated from only the largest and the smallest values.
Compare the data with the 18 and without it, and notice which calculation changes the moment that value is removed.
hintsEs: Las medidas de dispersión describen qué tan separados están los valores, no dónde está el centro.
Busca la medida que se calcula usando solamente el valor mayor y el menor.
Compara los datos con el 18 y sin él, y fíjate cuál cálculo cambia en el momento en que se quita ese valor.
choicesEs: El rango, porque es el valor más alto menos el más bajo
La mediana, porque está en el medio
La moda, porque es la más común
Solo la desviación media absoluta, nunca el rango

optional.label: Match each scouting question to the measure that answers it.

pairs.term: What was a typical game when one score is a record-breaking outlier?
pairs.termEs: ¿Cómo fue un juego típico cuando un puntaje es un récord atípico?

pairs.term: Which shoe size do most players wear?
pairs.termEs: ¿Qué talla de tenis usan la mayoría de los jugadores?

pairs.term: On a symmetric, outlier-free set, what is the average score?
pairs.termEs: En un conjunto simétrico y sin atípicos, ¿cuál es el puntaje promedio?

pairs.term: How far apart are the highest and lowest sprint times?
pairs.termEs: ¿Qué tan separados están el tiempo más alto y el más bajo?

optional.explanation: Each question names the job a different statistic does. A record-breaking outlier calls for the median, which resists extremes; "which one do most players wear" is the mode; a symmetric, outlier-free average is the mean; and the distance from the highest to the lowest sprint time is the range, a measure of spread rather than center.
optional.explanationEs: Cada pregunta nombra la tarea que hace una medida distinta. Un valor atípico que rompe récords pide la mediana, que resiste los extremos; "cuál usan la mayoría de los jugadores" es la moda; un promedio simétrico y sin valores atípicos es la media; y la distancia entre el tiempo de sprint más alto y el más bajo es el rango, una medida de dispersión y no de centro.
hints: Three of these answers describe the center of a data set and one describes how spread out it is — decide which job each question is asking about.
Sort by the wording: "most players wear" points to the value that repeats, "how far apart" points to a distance, and the two typical-value questions split on whether there is an outlier.
Start with the record-breaking outlier question. An extreme value pulls the mean but leaves the middle alone, so pick the measure that survives it, then take the shoe-size card.
hintsEs: Tres de estas respuestas describen el centro de un conjunto de datos y una describe qué tan dispersos están; decide qué tarea pide cada pregunta.

Clasifica por las palabras: "la mayoría de los jugadores usan" apunta al valor que se repite, "qué tan separados" apunta a una distancia, y las dos preguntas sobre el valor típico se separan según si hay un valor atípico.

Empieza con la pregunta del valor atípico que rompe récords. Un valor extremo jala la media pero deja el centro igual, así que elige la medida que lo resiste y luego toma la tarjeta del número de calzado.
optional.labelEs: Une cada pregunta de exploración con la medida que la responde.

optional.instructions: Sort each measure into whether it describes the CENTER of the data or the SPREAD of the data.
optional.explanation: Mean, median, and mode all answer "where is a typical value?", so they are measures of center. Range and mean absolute deviation answer "how spread out are the values?" — the range is the distance from the lowest value to the highest, and MAD is the average distance from the mean.
optional.explanationEs: La media, la mediana y la moda responden "¿dónde está un valor típico?", así que son medidas de centro. El rango y la desviación media absoluta responden "¿qué tan dispersos están los valores?": el rango es la distancia del valor más bajo al más alto, y la MAD es la distancia promedio respecto a la media.
hints: Two different questions live in this sort: one asks where the data sits, and one asks how far the values reach from each other.
A measure of center gives one typical value; a measure of spread describes distance or variation. Ask which question each word answers.
Start with Mean: it is the balancing point of the data, a single typical value, so it belongs in the center column. Now decide where Range goes.
hintsEs: En esta clasificación hay dos preguntas distintas: una pregunta dónde están los datos y otra qué tan lejos llegan los valores unos de otros.
Una medida de centro da un solo valor típico; una medida de dispersión describe distancia o variación. Pregúntate qué responde cada palabra.
Empieza con Media: es el punto de equilibrio de los datos, un solo valor típico, así que va en la columna de centro. Ahora decide dónde va Rango.
optional.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada medida según si describe el CENTRO de los datos o la DISPERSIÓN de los datos.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Analyst's Wrong Measure

workedExample.label: Data
workedExample.work: A player's points per game: 19, 21, 20, 22, 23, 2 (the 2 was a game cut short by an early ejection).
workedExample.workEs: Puntos por partido de un jugador: 19, 21, 20, 22, 23, 2 (el 2 fue un partido recortado por una expulsión temprana).

workedExample.label: Analyst's choice
workedExample.work: The analyst reports the mean (17.8) as the player's typical scoring because it uses all the data.
workedExample.workEs: El analista reporta la media (17.8) como el rendimiento típico porque usa todos los datos.

optional.correctWork: The analyst should report the median (20.5), not the mean. The score of 2 is an outlier from the cut-short game. It pulls the mean down to 17.8, which is lower than 5 of the 6 games, so it does not represent a typical performance. The median (20.5) is resistant to the outlier and better describes a typical game.
hints: Look at the value 2. Does it fit with the rest of the player's scores, or is it an outlier?
The mean (17.8) is lower than 5 of the 6 games. A good 'typical' value should sit among most of the data, like the median (20.5) does.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: la medida equivocada del analista
optional.explanation: The 2-point game was cut short by an ejection, so it is an outlier, and it drags the mean down to about 17.8 — lower than five of the six games. The median 20.5 sits among the 19-to-23 point games, so it describes the player's typical scoring much better.
optional.explanationEs: El partido de 2 puntos se acortó por una expulsión, así que es un valor atípico, y jala la media hasta cerca de 17.8, más bajo que cinco de los seis partidos. La mediana 20.5 queda entre los partidos de 19 a 23 puntos, así que describe mucho mejor la anotación típica del jugador.
optional.correctWorkEs: El analista debería reportar la mediana (20.5), no la media. El puntaje de 2 es un valor atípico del partido recortado. Jala la media hacia abajo hasta 17.8, que es menor que 5 de los 6 partidos, así que no representa un rendimiento típico. La mediana (20.5) resiste el valor atípico y describe mejor un partido típico.

approaching.stem: A gymnast's scores are: 8.5, 8.8, 8.7, 8.6, 8.9. There are no outliers. Which measure best represents a typical score?
choices: Mean
Median
Neither — the data is too small
Both are equally bad
approaching.explanation: The data is symmetric with no outliers, so the mean (8.7) best represents the typical score.
choiceFeedback: The median ignores how far apart the values are. Check whether this data has any outlier that would make leaving values out worthwhile.
Five values is plenty for a measure of center. A small set is only a problem when it contains extreme values.
Both measures actually work reasonably well here, since the scores are clustered close together. Decide which one uses the data most fully when there are no outliers.
hints: Look at the scores: 8.5 up to 8.9 — all five are bunched tightly together with no unusual value.
Rule of thumb: with no outliers and balanced data, one measure uses every value fairly. With outliers, the middle value is safer. Which case is this?
First step: check for an outlier — is any score far from the others? All five sit within 0.4 points, so apply the no-outlier rule.
approaching.stemEs: Las puntuaciones de una gimnasta son: 8.5, 8.8, 8.7, 8.6, 8.9. No hay valores atípicos. ¿Cuál medida representa mejor una puntuación típica?
approaching.explanationEs: Los datos son simétricos y no tienen valores atípicos, así que la media (8.7) representa mejor la puntuación típica.
choicesEs: La media
La mediana
Ninguna — hay muy pocos datos
Las dos son igual de malas
hintsEs: Mira los puntajes: de 8.5 a 8.9, los cinco muy juntos y sin ningún valor inusual.
Regla práctica: sin valores atípicos y con datos equilibrados, una medida usa todos los valores de forma justa. Con atípicos, el valor del medio es más seguro. ¿Cuál caso es este?
Primer paso: busca un atípico — ¿hay algún puntaje lejos de los demás? Los cinco están dentro de 0.4 puntos, así que aplica la regla de sin atípicos.

approaching.stem: A runner's mile times are: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. The 12:00 was due to a cramp. Which measure best represents a typical mile?
choices: Median — the outlier 12:00 pulls the mean too high
Mean — it uses all the data
Mode — it shows the most common time
Neither measure works
approaching.explanation: The 12:00 is an outlier that pulls the mean up. The median (7:15) better represents the runner's typical time.
choiceFeedback: Mean uses all data—but the outlier pulls it too high.
Mode shows most common—but doesn't handle the outlier well.
Both measures exist, but which resists the 12:00 outlier?
hints: Four times are near 7 minutes; one is 12:00 from a cramp. That 12:00 is an outlier, not a typical mile.
Ask: which measure gets dragged toward an extreme value, and which one just takes the middle of the ordered list?
First step: order the times and notice where 12:00 sits — far beyond the rest. Then choose the measure that isn't pulled by that extreme time.
approaching.stemEs: Los tiempos de una corredora en la milla son: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. El 12:00 se debió a un calambre. ¿Cuál medida representa mejor una milla típica?
approaching.explanationEs: El 12:00 es un valor atípico que sube la media. La mediana (7:15) representa mejor el tiempo típico de la corredora.
choicesEs: La mediana — el valor atípico de 12:00 sube demasiado la media
La media — usa todos los datos
La moda — muestra el tiempo más común
Ninguna medida sirve
hintsEs: Cuatro tiempos rondan los 7 minutos; uno es 12:00 por un calambre. Ese 12:00 es un valor atípico, no una milla típica.
Pregunta: ¿qué medida se deja arrastrar hacia un valor extremo y cuál simplemente toma el medio de la lista ordenada?
Primer paso: ordena los tiempos y fíjate dónde cae 12:00, muy lejos del resto. Luego elige la medida que ese tiempo extremo no jala.

approaching.stem: Match each data description with the best measure of center.
approaching.hint: Think about when you want to find what is typical—which measure handles outliers best?
hints: Scan each data list for a value that's wildly different from its neighbors — like one huge salary or one giant goal count.
Rule: outlier present → the middle value represents 'typical' better; no outlier → the average works fine. Decide outlier-or-not for each row.
Start with the salaries: $250K towers over the four values near $30K — a clear outlier. Match that row, then test the other three rows.
approaching.stemEs: Relaciona cada descripción de datos con la mejor medida de centro.
approaching.explanation: The shape of the data decides the measure. Symmetric data with no outliers is summarized well by the mean, data with an outlier or a long tail is summarized better by the median, and data made of categories leaves only the mode.
approaching.explanationEs: La forma de los datos decide la medida. Los datos simétricos y sin valores atípicos se resumen bien con la media, los datos con un valor atípico o una cola larga se resumen mejor con la mediana, y los datos formados por categorías solo permiten la moda.

approaching.stem: Data set: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. The mean is about 13.8 and the median is 7. Which better represents the typical value?
choices: Median (7) — the outlier 50 inflates the mean
Mean (13.8) — it includes all values
Both are equally good
Neither works for this data
approaching.explanation: The mean (13.8) is higher than 5 of the 6 values because the outlier 50 pulls it up. The median (7) better represents a typical value.
choiceFeedback: Mean uses all data—but 50 pulls it way above 5 of the 6 values.
Both exist, but which is closer to most of the data points?
One works well for typical value—use the one that resists 50.
hints: Five of the six values are between 5 and 8 — then there's 50. Notice where the mean (13.8) lands compared to those five.
Test for 'typical': count how many actual data values sit near 13.8, then how many sit near 7. A good measure stays close to most of the data.
First step: compare 13.8 to the list — it's bigger than 5, 6, 7, 7, AND 8. Ask what pulled it up there, and whether the median has that problem.
approaching.stemEs: Conjunto de datos: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. La media es aproximadamente 13.8 y la mediana es 7. ¿Cuál representa mejor el valor típico?
approaching.explanationEs: La media (13.8) es mayor que 5 de los 6 valores porque el valor atípico 50 la jala hacia arriba. La mediana (7) representa mejor un valor típico.
choicesEs: La mediana (7) — el valor atípico 50 infla la media
La media (13.8) — incluye todos los valores
Las dos son igual de buenas
Ninguna sirve para estos datos
hintsEs: Cinco de los seis valores están entre 5 y 8, y luego está el 50. Fíjate dónde cae la media (13.8) comparada con esos cinco.
Prueba qué es 'típico': cuenta cuántos datos reales están cerca de 13.8 y cuántos cerca de 7. Una buena medida se queda cerca de la mayoría de los datos.
Primer paso: compara 13.8 con la lista — es mayor que 5, 6, 7, 7 Y 8. Pregunta qué la jaló hasta allá y si la mediana tiene ese problema.

approaching.instructions: Sort each data feature into whether it suggests using the mean or the median.

categories.label: Use Mean
itemsEs: Los datos no tienen valores atípicos
Todos los valores están cercanos entre sí

categories.label: Use Median
items: Data has one or more outliers
Data is skewed to one side
One extreme value pulls the average
itemsEs: Los datos tienen uno o más valores atípicos
Los datos están sesgados hacia un lado
Un valor extremo jala el promedio

hints: The mean is sensitive to extreme values — outliers pull it up or down.
The median stays in the middle regardless of how extreme the highest or lowest values are.
approaching.label: Sort each feature by which measure of center it supports.
approaching.explanation: The mean uses every value, so a single extreme number drags it toward itself, while the median is just the middle of the ordered list and barely moves. That is why "no outliers," "symmetric," and "all values close together" point to the mean, and "has outliers," "skewed to one side," and "one extreme value pulls the average" point to the median.
approaching.explanationEs: La media usa todos los valores, así que un solo número extremo la jala hacia él, mientras que la mediana es simplemente el centro de la lista ordenada y casi no se mueve. Por eso "sin valores atípicos", "datos simétricos" y "todos los valores cercanos entre sí" apuntan a la media, y "tiene valores atípicos", "datos sesgados hacia un lado" y "un valor extremo jala el promedio" apuntan a la mediana.
approaching.labelEs: Clasifica cada característica según la medida de tendencia central que apoya.
hintsEs: La media es sensible a los valores extremos: los atípicos la jalan hacia arriba o hacia abajo.
La mediana se queda en el medio sin importar qué tan extremos sean el valor mayor o el menor.

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake — Forgetting to Order the Data

workedExample.label: Data
workedExample.workEs: Vueltas de un nadador: 9, 12, 8, 11, 10 (sin valores atípicos).

workedExample.label: Find the median
workedExample.work: The student keeps the numbers as written (9, 12, 8, 11, 10) and picks the middle one: median = 8.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante deja los números como están (9, 12, 8, 11, 10) y elige el del medio: mediana = 8.

workedExample.label: Choose a measure
workedExample.work: The student reports the median (8) as the typical lap count.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante reporta la mediana (8) como el número típico de vueltas.

approaching.correctWork: You must put the data in order before finding the median. In order: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. The middle value is 10, so the median is 10 (not 8). Since there are no outliers, the mean (10) and median (10) agree, and either is a fine measure of a typical lap.
hints: The median is the MIDDLE value only after the numbers are sorted from least to greatest.
Sort the data first: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. Now which value sits in the middle?
approaching.titleEs: Detecta el error: olvidar ordenar los datos
approaching.explanation: The median is the middle value only after the data is sorted. Ordering 9, 12, 8, 11, 10 gives 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, so the median is 10 — the 8 that was reported is actually the smallest value in the set. With no outliers here, the mean is also 10, so either measure describes a typical lap count.
approaching.explanationEs: La mediana es el valor del medio solo después de ordenar los datos. Ordenar 9, 12, 8, 11, 10 da 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, así que la mediana es 10; el 8 que se reportó en realidad es el valor más pequeño del conjunto. Como aquí no hay valores atípicos, la media también es 10, así que cualquiera de las dos medidas describe una cantidad típica de vueltas.
approaching.correctWorkEs: Debes ordenar los datos antes de buscar la mediana. En orden: 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. El valor del medio es 10, así que la mediana es 10 (no 8). Como no hay valores atípicos, la media (10) y la mediana (10) coinciden, y cualquiera es una buena medida de una vuelta típica.

onLevel.stem: A baseball player's batting averages over 6 seasons are: .280, .295, .290, .285, .300, .110. The .110 was an injury-shortened season. Which measure better represents the player's typical batting average?
choices: Median, because the .110 outlier pulls the mean down
Mean, because it uses all the data
Mean, because .110 is a real season
Neither measure works
onLevel.explanation: The .110 is an outlier that pulls the mean down to .260. The median (.2875) better represents typical performance because it isn't affected by the extreme value.
choiceFeedback: Mean uses all data—but the .110 outlier pulls it down.
Even though .110 is real, which measure shows typical performance better?
Both measures exist, but which resists the .110 outlier?
hints: Five seasons sit between .280 and .300; the .110 season is far below them — a low outlier.
A low outlier drags one measure DOWN below the player's usual level. Think about which measure uses only the middle of the ordered list.
First step: order the six averages and find the two middle ones. Notice that .110 sits at the far end and never touches that middle.
onLevel.stemEs: Los promedios de bateo de un jugador en 6 temporadas son: .280, .295, .290, .285, .300, .110. El .110 fue una temporada acortada por lesión. ¿Cuál medida representa mejor el promedio de bateo típico del jugador?
onLevel.explanationEs: El .110 es un valor atípico que baja la media hasta .260. La mediana (.2875) representa mejor el rendimiento típico porque no se ve afectada por el valor extremo.
choicesEs: La mediana, porque el valor atípico .110 baja la media
La media, porque usa todos los datos
La media, porque .110 es una temporada real
Ninguna medida sirve
hintsEs: Cinco temporadas están entre .280 y .300; la de .110 queda muy por debajo: un valor atípico bajo.
Un atípico bajo arrastra una medida HACIA ABAJO, por debajo del nivel habitual del jugador. Piensa qué medida usa solo el medio de la lista ordenada.
Primer paso: ordena los seis promedios y halla los dos del medio. Nota que .110 queda en el extremo y nunca toca ese medio.

editableCells.answer: Median (72 pulls the mean to 27.6, higher than 4 of 5 values)

hints: Row 2 swaps the last value for 72 — everything else matches Row 1. The table is built to show what one outlier does.
For each row: mean = sum ÷ 5, median = middle of the ordered list. Then ask if any value sits far from the pack before picking the best measure.
Row 1: add 15 + 18 + 16 + 17 + 15 and divide by 5; order the list to find the middle. Then rebuild both measures for Row 2 with the 72.
onLevel.explanation: The two rows differ only in the last value, which is what makes the effect of an outlier visible. Row 1 (15, 18, 16, 17, 15) has mean 81 ÷ 5 = 16.2 and median 16, so with no outlier the mean works fine. Row 2 swaps in 72: the mean jumps to 138 ÷ 5 = 27.6 while the median stays at 17, so the median is the better measure there.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las dos filas solo se diferencian en el último valor, y eso es lo que hace visible el efecto de un valor atípico. La fila 1 (15, 18, 16, 17, 15) tiene media 81 ÷ 5 = 16.2 y mediana 16, así que sin valor atípico la media funciona bien. La fila 2 cambia ese valor por 72: la media salta a 138 ÷ 5 = 27.6 mientras la mediana se queda en 17, así que ahí la mediana es la mejor medida.
hintsEs: La fila 2 cambia el último valor por 72; todo lo demás es igual que la fila 1. La tabla está hecha para mostrar qué hace un solo atípico.
Para cada fila: media = suma ÷ 5, mediana = el medio de la lista ordenada. Luego pregunta si algún valor queda lejos del grupo antes de elegir la mejor medida.
Fila 1: suma 15 + 18 + 16 + 17 + 15 y divide entre 5; ordena la lista para hallar el medio. Luego recalcula ambas medidas en la fila 2 con el 72.

onLevel.stem: Match the reason with whether to use mean or median.

pairs.left: Data is symmetric and has no extreme values
pairs.leftEs: Los datos son simétricos y sin valores extremos

pairs.left: Data has one or more outliers
pairs.leftEs: Los datos tienen uno o más valores atípicos

pairs.left: Data is skewed to one side
pairs.leftEs: Los datos están sesgados hacia un lado

pairs.left: All values are clustered close together
pairs.leftEs: Todos los valores están agrupados muy de cerca

onLevel.hint: Ask: if there is an outlier, which measure stays closer to most of the data?
hints: Each left card describes a data shape. Ask for each: could an extreme or lopsided value drag the average away from what's typical?
Rule: symmetric or tightly clustered → the mean works. Outliers or skew → the median resists the pull. Sort every card with that rule.
Start with 'Data has one or more outliers': an outlier always yanks the average, so pair that card with Use Median. Apply the rule to the rest.
onLevel.stemEs: Relaciona cada razón con el uso de la media o de la mediana.
onLevel.explanation: Reasons about using every value point to the mean, and reasons about protecting the summary from extreme values point to the median. Matching a reason to a measure is really asking whether outliers are present.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las razones que hablan de usar todos los valores apuntan a la media, y las razones que hablan de proteger el resumen de valores extremos apuntan a la mediana. Relacionar una razón con una medida es en realidad preguntar si hay valores atípicos.

onLevel.label: Data: 10, 12, 11, 13, 50. Place the mean (19.2) and median (12) on the number line. Notice how far apart they are because of the outlier.
hints: The mean (19.2) is pulled toward the outlier 50. The median (12) stays near the cluster of data.
When the mean and median are far apart, that is a sign of skewed data or an outlier.
onLevel.explanation: In the set 10, 12, 11, 13, 50 the mean is 96 ÷ 5 = 19.2 while the median is 12. On the line the mean sits far to the right, pulled toward the outlier 50, and the median stays inside the cluster from 10 to 13. A wide gap between the two markers is a signal that the data is skewed.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el conjunto 10, 12, 11, 13, 50 la media es 96 ÷ 5 = 19.2 mientras que la mediana es 12. En la recta, la media queda muy a la derecha, jalada por el valor atípico 50, y la mediana se queda dentro del grupo de 10 a 13. Una separación grande entre las dos marcas es una señal de que los datos están sesgados.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake — Choosing the Mean Despite an Outlier

workedExample.label: Data
workedExample.work: A receiver's catches per game: 12, 14, 13, 15, 11, 60 (the 60 was a record-setting playoff game).
workedExample.workEs: Recepciones por partido de un receptor: 12, 14, 13, 15, 11, 60 (el 60 fue un partido de playoffs de récord).

workedExample.label: Choose a measure
workedExample.work: The student reports the mean (≈ 20.8) as the typical number of catches because it uses every game.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante reporta la media (≈ 20.8) como el número típico de recepciones porque usa todos los partidos.

onLevel.correctWork: The student should report the median (13.5), not the mean. The 60-catch game is an outlier that pulls the mean up to about 20.8 — higher than 5 of the 6 games. The median (13.5) is resistant to that outlier and better represents a typical game.
hints: Compare the mean (≈ 20.8) to the actual games. Is it close to a typical value, or higher than almost all of them?
When one value (60) is far from the rest, it pulls the mean. The median (13.5) stays near the cluster, so it is the better choice.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error: elegir la media a pesar de un valor atípico
onLevel.explanation: Using every value is exactly the problem here: the 60-catch playoff game pulls the mean up to about 20.8, which is higher than five of the six games. The median 13.5 sits inside the cluster of 11 to 15 and is not moved by that extreme value, so it is the better report of a typical game.
onLevel.explanationEs: Usar todos los valores es justo el problema aquí: el partido de playoffs con 60 recepciones sube la media hasta cerca de 20.8, más alto que cinco de los seis partidos. La mediana 13.5 queda dentro del grupo de 11 a 15 y ese valor extremo no la mueve, así que representa mejor un partido típico.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante debería reportar la mediana (13.5), no la media. El partido de 60 recepciones es un valor atípico que jala la media hasta cerca de 20.8 — más alta que 5 de los 6 partidos. La mediana (13.5) resiste ese valor atípico y representa mejor un partido típico.

extending.title: Find the Reasoning Error

workedExample.label: Conclusion
workedExample.work: The mean (28.2) is the best measure because it uses all the data.
workedExample.workEs: La media (28.2) es la mejor medida porque usa todos los datos.

extending.correctWork: The median (32.5) is the better measure. The value 5 is an outlier (the player was injured that game) that pulls the mean down to 28.2, which is lower than any of the player's healthy games. The median (32.5) better represents typical minutes played.
hints: Look at the value 5. Does it fit with the rest of the data?
The mean (28.2) is lower than 5 of the 6 values. Does that seem like a 'typical' game?
extending.explanation: The value 5 is an outlier from an injury game, and it drags the mean down to 28.2 — lower than every healthy game in the set. The median 32.5 sits among the 30-to-35 minute games, so it describes typical minutes far better. Using all the data is not an advantage when one value is that extreme.
extending.explanationEs: El valor 5 es un valor atípico de un partido con lesión, y jala la media hasta 28.2, más bajo que cualquier partido sano del conjunto. La mediana 32.5 queda entre los partidos de 30 a 35 minutos, así que describe mucho mejor los minutos típicos. Usar todos los datos no es una ventaja cuando un valor es así de extremo.
extending.correctWorkEs: La mediana (32.5) es la mejor medida. El valor 5 es un valor atípico (el jugador se lesionó ese partido) que jala la media hasta 28.2, más baja que cualquiera de sus partidos sanos. La mediana (32.5) representa mejor los minutos típicos.

extending.prompt: A local newspaper reports that the average home price in a neighborhood is $450,000. The actual prices are: $180K, $200K, $190K, $210K, $195K, $1,725K. Is the reporter's claim misleading? Calculate the mean and median and explain which better represents a 'typical' home price.
extending.sentenceFrame: Mean = ___. Median = ___. The reporter's claim is ___ because the outlier ($1,725K) pulls the mean ___. The ___ (about $___) better represents a typical home price because ___.
extending.hint: Start by calculating both the mean and median—compare them to see if an outlier pulled mean.
hints: Five homes cost about $180K–$210K; one costs $1,725K. Check the reporter's $450,000 'average' against those five real prices.
Plan: (1) mean = sum of all six prices ÷ 6, (2) median = average of the 3rd and 4th ordered prices, (3) compare each to what most homes cost.
Step 1: add 180 + 200 + 190 + 210 + 195 + 1725 (in thousands) and divide by 6. Then order the six prices and average the middle two.
extending.explanation: The six prices add to $2,700K, so the mean is 2,700 ÷ 6 = $450K, matching the reporter — but the median is the average of the middle two prices, $195K and $200K, which is $197.5K. Five of the six homes cost between $180K and $210K, so the $1,725K home is an outlier pulling the mean far above what most homes cost. The claim is misleading, and the median better represents a typical price.
extending.explanationEs: Los seis precios suman $2,700K, así que la media es 2,700 ÷ 6 = $450K, igual que dice el reportero; pero la mediana es el promedio de los dos precios del medio, $195K y $200K, o sea $197.5K. Cinco de las seis casas cuestan entre $180K y $210K, así que la casa de $1,725K es un valor atípico que jala la media muy por encima de lo que cuestan casi todas. La afirmación es engañosa, y la mediana representa mejor un precio típico.
extending.promptEs: Un periódico local informa que el precio promedio de una casa en un vecindario es de $450,000. Los precios reales son: $180K, $200K, $190K, $210K, $195K, $1,725K. ¿Es engañosa la afirmación del reportero? Calcula la media y la mediana y explica cuál representa mejor el precio de una casa 'típica'.
hintsEs: Cinco casas cuestan entre $180K y $210K; una cuesta $1,725K. Revisa el 'promedio' de $450,000 del reportero contra esas cinco casas reales.
Plan: (1) media = suma de los seis precios ÷ 6, (2) mediana = promedio del 3.º y 4.º precio ordenados, (3) compara cada uno con lo que cuesta la mayoría.
Paso 1: suma 180 + 200 + 190 + 210 + 195 + 1725 (en miles) y divide entre 6. Luego ordena los seis precios y promedia los dos del medio.

extending.instructions: Sort each real-world situation into whether the mean or median is more commonly reported.

categories.label: Mean is typically reported
items: Average test score for a class (no outliers)
itemsEs: Calificación promedio de una clase (sin valores atípicos)

categories.label: Median is typically reported
items: Median household income in a city
Median home price in a neighborhood
itemsEs: Ingreso familiar mediano de una ciudad
Precio mediano de las casas de un vecindario

hints: Income and home prices often have extreme outliers (billionaires, mansions), so median is used.
Temperature and test scores are often symmetric, so mean works well.
extending.label: Sort by which measure is typically used in real life.
extending.explanation: Reports use the median when a few extreme values would distort the average. Household income and home prices have long tails — a few very high earners or very expensive houses — so the median is reported. Monthly temperature and an outlier-free set of class test scores are roughly symmetric, so the mean represents them well.
extending.explanationEs: Los reportes usan la mediana cuando unos pocos valores extremos distorsionarían el promedio. El ingreso familiar y los precios de las casas tienen colas largas (unos pocos ingresos muy altos o casas carísimas), así que se reporta la mediana. La temperatura mensual y un conjunto de calificaciones sin valores atípicos son bastante simétricos, así que la media los representa bien.
extending.labelEs: Clasifica según qué medida se usa normalmente en la vida real.
hintsEs: Los ingresos y los precios de casas suelen tener atípicos extremos (millonarios, mansiones), por eso se usa la mediana.
Las temperaturas y los puntajes de exámenes suelen ser simétricos, así que la media funciona bien.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Appropriate Measures is defaulting to the mean just because "it uses all the data," without first checking whether an outlier or skewed shape is present. For example, given a player's points per game 14, 16, 15, 17, 16, 58, a student calculates the mean (136 ÷ 6 ≈ 22.7) and reports that as the typical game — but 58 is far from the cluster of 14–17, so it pulls the mean above 5 of the 6 games. The median (16) actually represents a typical game here. Before choosing a measure, always scan the data for an outlier or a long tail first: only use the mean once you've confirmed the data has neither.

diagram.title: The Six Playoff Ticket Prices
diagram.caption: One courtside outlier towers over the rest — it drags the mean up to $85 even though the median ticket costs about $51.

connect.scenario: A sports reporter writes: 'The average ticket price for the playoffs is $85.' The actual prices are: $45, $50, $48, $52, $55, $260. The $260 ticket is a courtside seat.
connect.promptQuestion: Is $85 a fair way to describe a 'typical' ticket price? What measure should the reporter use?
connect.prompt: The reporter used the ___, which is ___. A better measure would be the ___ (about ___) because ___. The courtside seat at $260 is an ___ that pulls the mean ___.

check.stem: What is the mean ticket price?
check.explanation: The six prices total $510, and 510 ÷ 6 = $85 — matching the reporter's claim.

check.stem: What is the median ticket price?
check.explanation: In order: 45, 48, 50, 52, 55, 260. With 6 values the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th: (50 + 52) ÷ 2 = $51.

check.stem: Which measure better describes a 'typical' ticket?
choices: The median, because the $260 outlier pulls the mean far above most prices
The mean, because it uses every value
Neither — you should use the mode
The mean, because $85 is between the extremes
check.explanation: Five of the six tickets cost between $45 and $55. The single $260 courtside seat drags the mean up to $85, higher than every ordinary ticket. The median of $51 sits right where most prices actually are.

connect.modelAnswer: The reporter used the mean, $85 — but five of the six tickets cost between $45 and $55, so $85 is higher than almost every real ticket. The $260 courtside seat is an outlier that pulls the mean upward. The median, about $51, describes a typical ticket far better because it is not affected by one extreme value.

exitTicket.stem: Data set: 15, 18, 16, 17, 15, 72. Which measure of center best represents the data?
choices: Median, because 72 is an outlier
Mean, because it uses all values
Mean, because it is always best
Neither works for this data
exitTicket.explanation: The value 72 is an outlier. The mean (25.5) is pulled high by 72 and doesn't represent the typical values. The median (16.5) is a better measure of center.
choiceFeedback: True, but 72 pulls the mean up — an outlier distorts it.
Not always — a big outlier like 72 makes the median better.
One does work — the median resists the outlier 72.
hints: Scan the data: five values sit between 15 and 18, then one is 72. Ask yourself what that 72 does to an average.
One measure adds every value, so the 72 counts fully; the other uses only the middle of the ordered list. Decide which stays near most values.
First step: order the six values and locate the middle two — notice 72 sits at the far end. Then think about where the mean would land.

copyPanel.rule: Choosing Appropriate Measures of Center & Spread
steps: 1. Symmetric Data (No Outliers): Use Mean and MAD
2. Skewed Data (Has Outliers): Use Median and IQR (outliers distort the mean)
3. Compare distributions using both center (typical value) and spread (variability)
